title: Introduce density-axis tokens and migration adapter for legacy components
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Summary:
We need a single, programmatic "density" axis that scales core token families (color ramps, type scale, spacing/radius, shadow/elevation) so teams can opt into a compact/comfortable scale consistently across components. Alongside the new tokens, implement a migration adapter (token aliasing + runtime shim) that allows legacy components and older product routes to read new density-aware tokens without a big, synchronous rewrite.

Goals:
- Define the density axis: values = [compact, default, spacious] and mapping rules for each token family.
- Create token naming convention for density-aware tokens (e.g., color.primary.100@compact, type.base.scale@spacious).
- Produce a migration adapter spec for front-end runtime (CSS variable prefixes + JS token resolver) and a fallback strategy for server-rendered pages.
- Update core components: Button, Table row density, Card, and Chart overlay presets to consume new tokens.
- Provide an accessible contrast matrix for compact color ramps; meet WCAG 2.1 AA for text sizes across density variants.
- Deliver a rollout plan with canary routes, opt-in flags, and a deprecation schedule for legacy aliases.

Acceptance criteria:
- Token spec doc merged in Confluence with tables for color ramps, typographic scale, spacing, radii, and elevation deltas per density value.
- Figma token file updated and annotated; a reference page demonstrating compact vs default vs spacious across Button, Table, Chart and Form components.
- Migration adapter RFC reviewed by ENG and marked "approved for implementation". RFC must include pseudocode for variable resolution and an outline for server-side fallback.
- Engineering has a working prototype PR that toggles density via a query param and shows consistent visual parity with Figma.
- Accessibility signoff from a11y engineer for contrast and focus target sizes at the compact density.

Implementation notes / tradeoffs:
- We prefer a small finite set of density values (3) to avoid combinatorial explosion in design tokens and runtime complexity.
- Shadows/elevation will use an "elevation delta" approach: core elevation tokens remain, density adjusts the blur/spread/opacity via a delta map. This is cheaper than full token duplication for every surface.
- For charts, overlay and grid lines adopt density-aware opacity steps rather than full color remapping to preserve data readability.
- Migration adapter will expose both the new token keys and legacy aliases for 3 months after rollout, with automated lint rules to flag legacy alias usage.

Artifacts / links:
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/design-system-density (prototype frames annotated)
- Confluence PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DS/pages/32456/Density+Axis+PRD
- RFC (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-rfcs/pull/67
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/web/pull/4821

Risks / open questions:
- Token explosion: how do we keep token surface minimal while offering enough fidelity? (Design proposes deltas rather than full replication.)
- Server-rendered pages: how to surface density preference for SSR flows without flash-of-unstyled-density? (ENG to propose cookie + early-inserted CSS variables approach.)
- Chart readability at compact density for low-contrast data series — require product guidance on minimum contrast for charts.

Next steps:
- 2025-06-12: deliver first pass token tables (Aisha).
- 2025-06-18: cross-functional review with ENG (Carlos Vega) and PM (Lina Park).
- 2025-06-25: update Figma files and add three component demos (buttons, table rows, chart overlays).
- 2025-07-02: hand off RFC to ENG for prototype implementation.
